gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the full 4,000 to 4,500 W never comes out of one 120 V plug (a NEMA 5-20R outlet is 20 A, about 2,400 W; the TT-30R is 30 A, about 3,600 W; the full rating arrives only at 240 V on the L14-30R or summed across outlets), nor that a named reviewer measured the Anker S5000 kit's own two 400 W panels peaking at 680 W.
standout_why: Compared against three rival pages I opened. stormwatts.com/articles/240v-solar-generators-solar-input-compared (cited) gives PV voltage windows, panel Voc and series limits, but no outlet types, no outlet amp or watt limits and no measured panel output. stormwatts.com/articles/home-backup-flagship-power-stations-compared gives whole-unit watts and says the DELTA Pro 3's 120 V and 240 V buttons are mutually exclusive, but nothing per outlet. outletpowered.com/best/solar-generator-for-home-backup says the S5000 outputs 120 V or 240 V, not both at once, and names no outlet ratings. So rivals already hold the 120-or-240 rule and the PV windows; none holds the per-plug ceiling or a measured figure for kit panels. The us.ecoflow.com bundle pages ChatGPT cited returned HTTP 429 on both attempts, so I could not check them.
decides: It confirms the Anker SOLIX S5000 + 2× 400 W kit (ours, ships now, $3,599.99) as the pick for a shopper who means 4,000 W of output, with one caveat the page should state. The most a single 120 V plug gives is 3,600 W on the TT-30R or 2,400 W on a 5-20R; the full 4,500 W is on the 240 V L14-30R. The EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3 bundle has the same shape: 20 A and 30 A 120 V outlets, with 4,000 W reached only at 240 V (16.7 A) or across several outlets. A column 'most watts from one plug' would separate the rows. The kit panels are a refill source, not a 4,000 W source: 800 W rated is 18% of the S5000's 4,500 W, and ESS News measured 680 W peak from the same two panels, so the refill column should show about 6.3 h at rated output and about 7.4 h at the measured peak.
